name: Literature Review Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any literature review task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any literature review task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about literature review explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. When multiple literature review strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. When literature review guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Prefer explicit, readable literature review solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen literature review approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Keep literature review outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Measure before optimizing any literature review bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Before starting literature review work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to literature review (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Validate literature review outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Keep literature review changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic literature review advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated literature review concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new literature review abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting literature review assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about literature review over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
